title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame

sources.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
A Computational and Experimental Study of Coflow Laminar Methane/Air Diffusion Flames: Effects of Fuel Dilution, Inlet Velocity, and Gravity

key_findings: Characterized the behavior of weak coflow diffusion flames of methane and ethylene, as a function of velocity and fuel dilution, through measurement of flame shape, lift-off heights, temperatures and extinction limits.

Characterized the sooting tendencies of diffusion flames with long residence times, as a function of velocity and fuel dilution, through measurement of flame shape, gas temperatures in the soot-free portion of the flame, soot luminosity, soot temperatures, and soot volume fractions.
fields.earth_applications: Understanding of those factors that affect flame extinction in diffusion flames is critical in the suppression of fires and in improving engine efficiency.

paper_findings.text: The flames become longer and wider as buoyancy is eliminated or fuel concentration is increased.
The computed temperature profiles and measured soot temperatures are modeled accurately.
The influences of varying inlet velocity are correctly captured.

conditions.label: CH4-air diffusion flames, normal gravity (1g)
evidence: Eighteen flames have been studied under both microgravity (μg) and normal gravity (1g) (36 flames total): three fuel dilution levels (40%, 70%, and 100% CH4 in mole fractions) and six inlet velocities (approximately 24, 46, 55, 64, 80, 89 cm/s, changing slightly at different fuel dilutions)

key_findings: The flames become longer and wider as buoyancy is eliminated or fuel concentration is increased.
